newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska to proceed with new share issue.
newsitem.headline: Skanska to proceed with new share issue.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska said on Friday its board would go ahead with a new issue of B-series shares, approved by an extraordinary meeting of shareholders in May in connection with a redemption programme.

Skanska said the aim of the new shares was to enable the company to raise an amount at least equal to the sum by which its capital stock will be reduced as a result of an upcoming share redemption, that is 10 crowns per redeemed share.
The new issue price has been set at 345.32 crowns a share which is the average volume-weighted price paid for a Skanska B share between July 9-15 this year.
Skanska shares on Thursday closed at 356.5 crowns.
The number of newly issued shares totalled 359,222 which means Skanska raised 124.3 million crowns, Skanska said in a statement.
Skanska said the board also decided to propose to an extraordinary meeting of shareholders on August 4 that the final amount of the capital stock reduction be 124.3 million crowns.
The total redemption amount, based on shares submitted in response to the voluntary share redemption offer, is 4.97 billion crowns.
In addition the board decided to propose that the meeting adopt a resolution approving a bonus issue increasing the par value of each Skanska share to 12 from 10 crowns.
"These steps will restore Skanska's capital stock, thereby simplifying the redemption process," Skanska said.
